text:
By Saumya Khanduja ,
55 minutes ago
Feb 24, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray (5) brings the ball up court against the Golden State Warriors during the first half at Smoothie King Center. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images
Upon his return, Dejounte Murray was far from quiet and cautious. After more than a year away from NBA action because of a ruptured right Achilles tendon, the veteran guard made his 2025-26 season debut in the New Orleans Pelicans‚Äô 113-109 victory over the Golden State Warriors.
While his individual performance was encouraging, his ambitious outlook for the remainder of the season truly defined the night.
Dejounte Murray Sets Sights on an Unlikely Play-In Push Murray understands the reality of the Pelicans‚Äô situation. The team is 17-42 and sitting 11 games behind the 10th seed in the Western Conference with just 23 contests remaining.
New Orleans faces extremely long odds to qualify for the Play-In Tournament. Still, Murray made it clear he would not concede the season. He took to X with his blunt honesty and unwavering belief about his postseason push goals.
‚ÄúDuh!!! Are we a contender? No. Can we reach the top 6 spot? No. Can we build some momentum playing together and build winning habits rest of the season? Yes. Can we treat every game like a championship game and win, win, win? Yes. Can we get in them last spots in the play-in??? Du .‚Äù
Mathematically, the climb is steep. Historically, the fewest wins by a play-in team came during the 2020-21 season with 34 victories. To reach that threshold, the Pelicans would likely need to finish the season 17-6. It‚Äôs an ambitious pace, something they have not sustained all year.
Nevertheless, New Orleans has little incentive to tank, as it does not control its 2026 first-round pick. For Murray, competing now is more valuable than positioning for the lottery. He wants every remaining game treated with postseason intensity, regardless of the standings.
Murray Bluntly Denies Trade Rumors In addition to outlining his goals for the stretch run, Murray addressed speculation that he had requested a trade before the deadline. Reports circulated suggesting the 29-year-old preferred a change of scenery, but he quickly and emphatically rejected that narrative.
‚ÄúLET‚ÄôS CLEAR THE AIR CAUSE F*** A SOURCE,‚Äù Murray posted on social media . ‚ÄúMe Or My Agent Never Requested A Trade Out Of NEW ORLEANS!!!! Joe And The Whole Organization Know I Was Locked In To Come Back Better Than Ever To Help Make This Play In Push And Whatever Comes After That!! It‚Äôs Bouts To Get Fun!!‚Äù
His response left little room for ambiguity.
Considering that he previously expressed frustration with how aspects of his recovery were handled last season, his public support of the franchise, including executive vice president Joe Dumars, is significant.
Encouraging Debut After a Long Recovery On the court, Murray‚Äôs return was measured but impactful. He logged 25 minutes, finishing with 13 points on 5-of-11 shooting, along with 3 assists, 2 rebounds, and 1 steal. Most notably, he converted a crucial layup with just over a minute remaining to extend New Orleans‚Äô lead and help secure the win.
Beyond the numbers, his movement appeared fluid, and his conditioning looked strong for a player coming off one of basketball‚Äôs most challenging injuries. Achilles recoveries are notoriously difficult, and there were understandable questions about whether he would regain his pre-injury form.
After the game, Murray expressed gratitude and hunger in equal measure.
‚ÄúIt was great. The win matters, though,‚Äù he said. ‚ÄúI‚Äôm hungry. I want the fans to know I‚Äôm hungry. I‚Äôm not suiting up for me, I‚Äôm suiting up for this organization, my brothers, and the fans. We want to build momentum going into the offseason and next year.‚Äù
The Pelicans‚Äô disappointing season has been shaped largely by injuries and inconsistency rather than a lack of talent.
With Murray back in the lineup and key players nearing full health, New Orleans finally has an opportunity to evaluate what this roster looks like at something closer to full strength.
